rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> Hydrus-2d simulations plus greenhouse lysimeter experiments (bare soil and sweet corn) on Kidman sandy loam with continuous vs 2-d pulsed drip fertigation. Q2: Abstract and Conclusion <U+2013> continuous low-rate application through a buried point source (dripper) gave greater P mobility and higher soil solution/extractable P around emitters than intermittent application; extractable P near the source 20-25% higher in bare soil. Q3: 'Comparison of Simulation and Lysimeter Results' <U+2013> both the Hydrus-2d simulation (Fig. 4) and direct bicarbonate-extractable P sampling of lysimeter soil (Fig. 5) showed zones of higher available P under continuous application. Q4: Methods and Results <U+2013> soil moisture monitored by tensiometers and gravimetric sampling (Fig. 3, Fig. 5); soil around emitters was wetter under continuous treatment, the moisture condition through which P is kept in solution and mobile. Q8: 'Comparison of Simulation and Lysimeter Results' and Conclusion <U+2013> modelled soluble P and measured extractable P not directly comparable; model idealised soil, ignored variability and preferential flow/surfacing; Langmuir isotherm an inadequate model for P sorption during transport; effect on soil P not evident when corn was grown with low P in irrigation water; future work needed on other crops and soils.
rows.notes: Study is on continuous vs intermittent drip (point-source) fertigation, matching the passage's frequent-irrigation/high-moisture mechanism. Q3 is a qualified yes: simulation and measurement are independent approaches that converge, but the model was not calibrated against the measurements and the authors note distribution differences. Q7 no: the finding that the soil-P difference disappeared under cropping with low P concentration is reported as variation, not stated as a requirement. Q9 no: Figs 5 and the reported soil-P ranges are spatial distributions, not replicate dispersion; standard deviations are given only for biomass and tissue P (Figs 6, 8), not for the soil P availability result. Single soil (Kidman sandy loam), one crop, greenhouse lysimeters only.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> own Hydrus-2d simulations and greenhouse lysimeter experiments with triplicate lysimeters per treatment. Q2: Abstract and 'Distribution of Plant-Available Phosphorus <U+2013> No Uptake' (Fig. 5) <U+2013> bicarbonate (Olsen) extractable P immediately around the point source was 20-25% higher under continuous than pulsed fertigation on bare soil, with higher concentrations and greater downward transport. Q3: 'Comparison of Simulation and Lysimeter Results' <U+2013> Hydrus-2d solution-P isolines (Fig. 4, ~25 mg/L continuous vs ~20 mg/L 2-d) and direct soil extraction (Fig. 5) both indicated zones of higher available P under continuous application. Q4: Methods/Results <U+2013> soil water content measured (tensiometers, gravimetric sampling, Fig. 5) and simulated (Fig. 3); continuous treatment kept soil around emitters wetter, the intermediate moisture condition for P mobility. Q8: 'Comparison of Simulation and Lysimeter Results' and 'Uptake of Phosphorus by Young Corn Plants' <U+2013> simulated and measured P not directly comparable; model limitations (idealised soil, no preferential flow, inadequate Langmuir sorption model); the extractable-P advantage was not evident in the cropped lysimeters where continuous treatment actually had lower soil extractable P; conclusion calls for tests on other crops and soil types.
rows.notes: The 20-25% extractable-P increase is the study's own bare-soil lysimeter result; the passage attributes it to drip fertigation, which matches the buried point-source emitter set-up. Q3 is a qualified yes (simulation plus measurement). Q7 no: no condition stated as a requirement from own findings. Q9 no: no standard deviation, CI or replicate range reported for the 20-25% soil-P difference; only spatial isocharts and spatial concentration ranges. Only one soil, one crop, greenhouse lysimeter scale; 14-d bare-soil run.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Primary study combining Hydrus-2d simulation with greenhouse lysimeter experiments on one calcareous sandy loam; three replicate lysimeters per treatment. Note the cropped experiment contradicts the bare-soil soil-P result (extractable P lower under continuous fertigation with corn), though plant P uptake and biomass were higher.
